subject: radiology
title: TIPS selection: who benefits, who breaks

steps.tx: Patient selection decides shunt success, because only refractory portal complications justify the risks of diversion. **Refractory variceal bleeding** that defeats bands and drugs earns urgent shunt placement and portal pressure falls directly. **Refractory ascites** that needs frequent large volume taps suits an elective shunt that returns fluid toward circulation. **Budd Chiari syndrome** with failed anticoagulation can open through shunt restoration of hepatic outflow in selected patients. Portal **hydrothorax** also drains back once the gradient falls after successful shunt creation in hospital.
steps.say: Patient selection decides shunt success because only refractory portal complications justify the risks of diversion. Variceal bleeding that defeats bands and drugs earns urgent shunt placement and pressure falls directly. Refractory ascites that needs frequent taps suits an elective shunt that returns fluid toward circulation. Hepatic outflow blockage with failed anticoagulation can open through shunt restoration in selected patients. Chest fluid from portal pressure also drains back once the gradient falls after creation.

steps.tx: This portogram shows a **stent graft** that connects the **portal vein** below with the **hepatic vein** and cava above. The label records a **fallen portosystemic gradient** below twelve, which marks successful decompression after shunt creation. That pressure fall explains why refractory bleeding and ascites improve when selection chooses a patient with adequate reserve. The image matters for the exam because anatomy alone never justifies a shunt without reserve assessment. Bilirubin, severity score, heart function and tumour screening all gate the decision beforehand.

steps.tx: A sick liver tolerates diversion poorly, so reserve markers warn the team before any shunt puncture. **Bilirubin above roughly 4 mg per dL** combined with a high **MELD score** warns of liver failure after shunting. **Recurrent overt encephalopathy** predicts worse confusion once ammonia bypasses the liver through a new channel. **Heart failure with pulmonary hypertension** decompensates when shunt flow floods the right heart suddenly after deployment. Polycystic livers and active infection block needle paths and risk seeding the graft with organisms.
steps.say: A sick liver tolerates diversion poorly so reserve markers warn the team before any shunt puncture. High bilirubin combined with a high severity score warns of liver failure after shunting. Recurrent overt confusion is a warning because it predicts worse confusion once ammonia bypasses the liver. Heart failure with lung hypertension decompensates when shunt flow floods the right heart suddenly. Cystic livers and active infection block needle paths and risk seeding the graft.

steps.tx: Workup precedes every shunt puncture, because unmasked heart or tumour disease turns benefit into harm quickly. **Cardiac echo** excludes pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure that a shunt would unmask after deployment. Triphasic imaging screens for **hepatocellular tumour** that a needle could seed or a shunt could bypass unsafely. **MELD and Child Pugh scoring** quantifies reserve so consent reflects real risk for that patient honestly. The team also reviews lactulose and rifaximin because brain preparation lowers ammonia load before diversion rises.

steps.tx: Consent for a shunt weighs survival months against confusion, and that trade needs explicit documentation beforehand. **Survival gains** in refractory bleeding and ascites trade against **encephalopathy risk** that approaches one in three patients. Acceleration of **liver failure** in marginal reserve needs frank discussion with the transplant team before puncture. Bands, taps and transplant listing frame alternatives honestly so the patient sees every reasonable path clearly. **Documented goals** align the shunt with what the patient values most in remaining life.
